issue.title: lastcall: {count} {noun} for {project} (audit of {sha})
issue.intro: Valid findings that lastcall did not turn into a pull request: they need your decision, or they are too large for one. Close this issue when you have decided.
plan.title: lastcall: {count} {noun} for {project} (improvement plan at {sha})
plan.intro: Improvements that lastcall checked against the code. Tick the ones you want: lastcall builds each one as a pull request, verified by your tests, in its next run on this project. Close this issue when you are done with it: the ideas you did not tick are dropped.
pr.footer: lastcall: audit of `{sha}` with {engine}; findings {ids}; implemented with {model} ({effort}); {checked}; secret scan: clean.
pr.idea.footer: lastcall: idea {ids} of the improvement plan {plan}; implemented with {model} ({effort}); {checked}; secret scan: clean.
pr.conflict: This pull request no longer merges cleanly into {branch}. lastcall closed it: what it changed goes back to pending, and a later run makes the change again on the current code.
revert.title: Revert "{title}"
revert.body: lastcall watched {url} after its merge, and {reason}. This pull request reverts {sha}. Merge it if that change is the cause, or close it if it is not. lastcall paused the project: activate it again on the Projects page.
watch.checks: the checks of the merged commit failed ({names}), where they passed before it
watch.health: {address} stopped answering ({count} checks in a row)
pr.ticket.footer: Fixes #{number}. lastcall: issue #{number}, labelled `lastcall`; implemented with {model} ({effort}); {checked}; secret scan: clean.
pr.tests.footer: lastcall: tests for `{sha}` with {engine}; findings {ids}; written with {model} ({effort}); {checked}; they change only tests; secret scan: clean.
pr.deps.footer: lastcall: dependency upgrades for `{sha}` with {engine}; findings {ids}; made with {model} ({effort}); {checked}; secret scan: clean.
ticket.stuck:
lastcall worked on this issue and stopped: {why}

Once the issue says what was missing, add the label `lastcall` again.
ticket.red: its change did not pass the project's checks, twice.
ticket.secrets: the secret scan stopped its change.
check.tests: tests run again in a clean container: `{line}`
check.tests.image: tests run again in a clean {image} container: `{line}`
check.build: the project has no tests: a clean container only checked that the code compiles
suggest.no-tests: no tests: fixes can only be checked to build
suggest.environment: {language}: add a .lastcall.yml with its environment, or a devcontainer
suggest.no-language: no main language: add a .lastcall.yml with its environment
suggest.large: large: an audit covers part of the code
suggest.truncated: very many files: size is a lower bound

web.dest.telegram.step1: In Telegram, open @BotFather, send it /newbot and follow its steps. At the end it gives you the bot's token.
web.dest.telegram.step2: Open your new bot and press Start, or send it any message.
web.dest.telegram.step3: Paste the token here and press Find my chat.
web.dest.telegram.chat_hint: Press Find my chat, or write the ID if you know it.
web.dest.telegram.none: Your bot has no recent messages. Send it any message in Telegram, then press Find my chat again.
web.dest.telegram.bad_token: Telegram does not accept that token. Copy it again from @BotFather.

web.dest.telegram.webhook: This bot uses a webhook, so lastcall cannot read its messages. Write the chat ID by hand.
web.dest.ntfy.step1: Install the ntfy app on your phone (Android or iOS), or open ntfy.sh in your browser.
web.dest.ntfy.step2: Subscribe to the topic below. It is random on purpose: anyone who knows a topic's name can read it.

web.dest.slack.step1: In Slack, add an incoming webhook to the channel: create an app at api.slack.com/apps and turn on Incoming Webhooks.

web.dest.email.to: Send to, if it is another address

web.runs.fanout: When several accounts burst at the same time, they review the same project together, and one judge keeps what holds.
web.runs.fanout_hint: Each account's reviewers spend that account's quota; the judge and the fixes spend the quota of the one with the most left. A subscription bursts only in the two days before its reset, so two that reset on different days rarely meet. To combine your accounts at any time, choose “All free accounts, one judge” in Audit now, on the Projects page.
